headline: Delhi Airport Security Installs 'Complimentary Bomb' Kiosk to Streamline Threat Processing
body:
In a move aimed at reducing the administrative burden on intelligence agencies, the Delhi International Airport has introduced a self-service kiosk where passengers can register their mandatory Independence Day bomb threats electronically before heading to the check-in counter.

The initiative, dubbed 'Operation Constant Panic,' allows travelers to select their preferred threat intensity—ranging from 'Mildly Concerning' to 'Total Chaotic Shutdown'—directly via a touchscreen interface. Airport authorities hope this will prevent the traditional bottleneck of last-minute emailed threats causing unscheduled evacuation drills.

'Processing a bomb threat manually takes an entire afternoon of paperwork and panic,' explained an airport spokesperson who requested anonymity to avoid being promoted to a desk job. 'With the new system, we print a token, send out a standard tweet about being on high alert, and everyone goes back to their lattes within forty-five minutes. It’s efficiency at its peak.'

The airport has also integrated a loyalty program, offering frequent threat-emitters a complimentary beverage voucher at the terminal cafe. While critics argue this may incentivize more threats, the airport management maintains that it is simply providing a structured outlet for the annual surge in civic anxiety.
